profile.reading: Per Digital Realty own site, this Austin, Texas facility (AUS11) sits at 7500 Metro Center Drive and totals 85,500 square feet across 2 stories, with N+1 UPS and N+1 cooling redundancy. The facility is SOC2, SOC3, and PCI-DSS certified, runs on 100 percent renewable energy, and holds CEEDA Gold and Energy Star certification. No power capacity in MW is published on this page.

reading.body:
Digital Realty Austin AUS11 publishes no megawatt capacity figure, making its relevance to AI scaling impossible to assess from official sources. The facility totals 85,500 square feet across two stories with N+1 redundancy on power and cooling, certifications for security and compliance work, and a stated commitment to 100 percent renewable energy. Without power capacity disclosed, this campus cannot be ranked among Texas facilities or compared to the scaling demands of AI training infrastructure.

Texas has published power capacity at 18 of its 133 mapped data center facilities, totaling 468 megawatts. AUS11's operator Digital Realty reports capacity at other Texas sites but has chosen not to publish a figure for this Austin location. The absence of a disclosed megawatt rating places this facility outside the ranked set of published capacity in the state.

Whether AUS11 matters to AI depends on unpublished facts: its actual power draw, the density and mix of compute it hosts, and whether any portion of it is allocated to large language model training or inference. The certifications and redundancy indicate capability for regulated workloads, but certifications do not distinguish AI-grade infrastructure from general-purpose colocation. The facility exists and is operational, but its role in the AI compute landscape remains opaque.
